The tumpong (called inci by the Maranao) is a Philippine bamboo flute, an aerophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 421.111.12. It is about half the size of the largest bamboo flute, the palendag, and is built like it as a lip-valley flute: the player blows across the bamboo lip set at the top, so that the airstream passes over the top hole and sounds. The instrument is used mostly by the Maguindanao and is their commonest flute; it is usually played at family gatherings in the evening and is regarded as a masculine instrument.

暫通翁主要由竹管製成，竹材作為樂器主體提供溫暖的音質共鳴。樂器頂部設有竹製簧片，: The tumpong is made mainly of bamboo; the bamboo forms the body and gives a warm resonance. At the top of the instrument sits a bamboo lip, carefully shaped so that it vibrates and sounds. The fingerholes are cut into the bamboo tube, and the airstream is controlled precisely to set pitch and timbre. The whole structure makes the most of the natural properties of bamboo and needs no metal or leather fittings, which keeps the craft traditional and shows the Maguindanao's handling of natural materials.
暫通翁具有明亮而穿透力強的音色，音質帶有溫暖的竹製樂器特有的質感。樂器音域位於中: The tumpong has a bright, strongly penetrating timbre, with the warm texture particular to bamboo instruments. Its range lies in the upper middle register, the tone is clear and open, and at an evening family gathering it carries a long way. Its resonance rests on the air vibrating inside the bamboo tube, the airstream at the top hole giving rich overtones. Compared with the steadier, lower sound of the larger palendag, the tumpong is lighter and more lively; compared with other Southeast Asian bamboo flutes it keeps the natural warmth of the bamboo flute while its moderate size gives it a flexible expressiveness. The sound of this masculine instrument penetrates well and suits playing outdoors.
暫通翁是菲律賓南部摩根達瑙人的傳統竹製長笛，起源於民達那峨島的穆斯林文化區域。這: The tumpong is a traditional bamboo flute of the Maguindanao of the southern Philippines, from the Muslim cultural region of Mindanao. The instrument has passed down through generations in Maguindanao communities and is an important part of their musical culture. It follows the lip-valley flute design: the player sounds it by blowing across the bamboo lip at the top, and the airstream passing the holes gives its distinctive timbre. Compared with its sister instrument the palendag, the tumpong is smaller and easier to carry and play. In Maguindanao daily life it is played mainly at family gatherings in the evening, and its strong, full tone has made it the people's commonest flute. Over time the craft of making it and the tradition of playing it have been kept and passed on within Maguindanao communities, a reflection of the musical heritage and cultural identity of the Muslim peoples of the Philippines.
